prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added the `heading_offset` option (whole number 0–5, default 0, anything else raises `ValueError`) and the `--heading-offset N` command-line flag; the full test suite passes. A new tree processor runs before all other tree processors and shifts every h1–h6 Markdown produces, stopping at h6. That covers hash, underline and `md_in_html` headings, and `toc` sees the shifted levels in its tokens and `toc_depth`. Raw HTML headings that pass through unprocessed are not shifted. Headings an extension adds later, in its own tree processor, would not be shifted either. True, floats and strings are rejected; out-of-range CLI values give a usage error. I added tests and documented the option in the library, CLI and `toc` docs, with a changelog entry under [Unreleased].
